questions.stem: A 48-year-old female patient complains of dry mouth and dryness of the eyes. Her investigation showed the presence of anti-SS-A & anti-SS-B antibodies. Which of the following drugs would help in managing this patient’s dryness of mouth?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cevimeline
  • A 48-year-old female patient with complaints of dry mouth and dryness of eyes and investigation showing the presence of anti-SS-A or anti-SS-B antibodies point towards a diagnosis of Sjogren’s syndrome.
  • Cevimeline is a muscarinic agonist that preferentially activates M1 and M3 receptors on lacrimal and salivary gland epithelia. The drug has a long-lasting sialogogic action and may have fewer side effects and better patient compliance than pilocarpine.
  • Hence, this drug would help in managing this patient’s symptoms


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 153, 159.

questions.stem: Mr. Zee, aged 38 years, comes to the OPD with complaints of drooping of eyelids, difficulty while chewing food, and weakness of upper and lower limbs, which fluctuates in intensity over time. The physician wants to confirm myasthenia gravis. The drug used to diagnose this condition is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Edrophonium
  • It is a short-acting Anticholinesterase
  • It is used in the diagnosis of myasthenia gravis
  • Differentiate between cholinergic & myasthenia crises.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 172, 174.

He was given pyridostigmine for the treatment and after a few days, the patient had increased salivation and diarrhea. Which drug is used to control the symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: A 58-year-old patient had laryngeal cancer for that she went neck irradiation. After that, she developed a dry mouth and decreased salivary secretion. Which of the following drug is not useful in the above condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glycopyrrolate
  • Drugs used for dry mouth/ Sjogren’s are cholinergic drugs such as
  • Cevimeline
  • Anticholinesterase drugs
  • Pilocarpine
  • Glycopyrrolate (Option B) is an anticholinergic drug with M3 receptor blocking action at the glands, which itself leads to dryness of the mouth
  • Glycopyrrolate is used:
  • As a pre-anesthetic medication to decrease secretions (a quaternary compound that does not cross BBB)
  • To reduce salivary, tracheobronchial, and pharyngeal secretions & gastric secretions; and
  • To block cardiac vagal inhibitory reflexes during induction of anesthesia and intubation


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 152, 153, 157

questions.stem: A 55-year-old farmer was brought to casualty with symptoms of severe abdominal cramps with vomiting, diarrhea, profuse lacrimation, and salivation. His BP was 80/60 mm Hg. Pupillary constriction is marked. The drug used in the management of the above poisoning is which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Atropine
  • Atropine is used to treat myopia and inflammation in the eyes (uveitis or iritis). It is also used for the eye examination and diagnose eye problems like blurred vision or squint in children


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 116, 122

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female was brought to casualty with symptoms of vomiting, diarrhea, profuse lacrimation, salivation, and miosis. She had taken an OP compound to commit suicide. She was immediately started on atropine and the junior resident in the medicine department was told to watch for signs of atropinization. Which of the following is an indicator of adequate atropinisation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pupillary dilation
  • Indicators of adequate atropinization are an increase in heart rate (Not decrease – Option A), pupillary dilation (commonly used criteria), and absence of secretions


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 123

questions.stem: A 23-year-old male Mr. X was brought to the emergency room by his father. When the father was asked about history, the father told that Mr. X ate some seeds from a plant and started behaving crazy. On examination he was confused, his skin was hot and dry. His pupils were dilated and unresponsive to light. Blood pressure was 180/105 mm Hg, pulse 150/min, and rectal temperature 40 C (104 F). The treatment of choice for the above poisoning is which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Physostigmine
  • This is a case of atropine poisoning probably from datura seeds
  • Confusion, hot and dry skin, tachycardia, pupils dilated, and high-temperature point toward datura poisoning
  • Datura stramonium is a widespread annual plant, containing atropine, hyoscyamine, and scopolamine, which can produce poisoning with a severe anticholinergic syndrome.
  • Teenagers ingest the roots, seeds, or the entire plant to obtain its hallucinogenic and euphoric effects
  • Physostigmine 5–2 mg i.v is the specific antidote for atropine poisoning
  • It crosses the blood-brain barrier and antagonizes both central and peripheral actions
  • Neostigmine and pyridostigmine don’t cross BBB


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 122

questions.stem: A 70-year-old male came with complaints of impaired gait or movement, language difficulties, low energy, memory loss, and mood swings. Investigations revealed positive amyloid on PET imaging and an increase in CSF total tau and phospho-tau. Which drug used in the management of the above condition is not a cholinergic drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Memantine
  • This is a case of Alzheimer’s disease
  • Option A. Rivastigmine, Option B. Donepezil & Option C. Galantamine are anticholinesterasesthat increase ACh levels in the brain. Hence. They are used for Alzheimer’s disease
